flawed_step: The key invariant 'a vertex's distance is final when it is extracted' cannot be justified. The proof needs δ(y) ≤ δ(u) for the first unsettled vertex y on a shortest s–u path, which uses the non-negativity of the path segment from y to u. With negative edges (even with no negative cycles) that segment can have negative weight, so the step fails.
counterexample: Digraph with edges s→a (2), s→b (4), b→a (−3), a→c (1). It has no cycles. True distances: δ(a)=1, δ(b)=4, δ(c)=2. Trace: extract s, giving d[a]=2 and d[b]=4; extract a (2) and settle it, giving d[c]=3; extract c (3) and settle it; extract b (4). Relaxing b→a would give 1, but a is settled and never re-inserted, so c stays at 3. Reported d[c]=3 ≠ 2 (and d[a]=2 ≠ 1 unless the settled label is overwritten).
assessment_summary: The statement is false. Label-setting Dijkstra is correct only when every edge weight is non-negative, because the finality-at-extraction invariant depends on it. Ruling out negative cycles is not enough: a small acyclic digraph with one negative edge makes the textbook algorithm report a wrong distance.
